transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-09-21
- Time: 14:30 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Evelyn Grant (Archon Head of ML); Marcus Liu (Archon Infra); Olivia Park (Finance); Tom Reyes (PM)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): Archon is evaluating Redwood for an LLM inference platform. Primary focus is cost/unit economics (per-token pricing), tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, and operational levers (batching, KV cache, quantization). They have strict budget targets and procurement timeline end of month. Security (SOC2, KMS, SSO) is required. Next steps: pricing deck, benchmarking plan, SOC2 docs, schedule deep dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros? We got about 40 minutes, want to focus on cost economics and the levers that move the needle.
[00:07] Evelyn (Archon): Hi all, Evelyn here. We're leading model ops and want to understand per-token unit costs across your hosted API vs dedicated clusters or private deployments. Also how batching and caching affects our monthly spend.
[00:17] Marcus (Archon): Marcus — infra. My team's worried about network egress and private data retention. Also curious how much ops overhead for private would be vs just using hosted.
[00:27] Liam: Great. Priya from our SE team will dig into perf and batching. Priya?
[00:31] Priya (Redwood SE): Hey all. High level: hosted is fastest to go live, pay-as-you-go. Dedicated gives predictable throughput with reserved capacity and lower unit cost at scale. Private is full control but more ops work and a platform fee. Key levers: batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization profiles, model selection, and request routing.
[00:50] Tom (Archon PM): When you say "unit cost," do you mean per generated token or end-to-end cost including pre- and post-processing?
[00:56] Priya: Primarily per-token CPU/GPU compute cost for generation, but we also want to account for added tokenization, prompt prep tokens, and embedding costs if you use rerank. We'll show examples.
[01:08] Evelyn: Our baseline: 2 million inference requests/month, avg prompt 180 tokens, response 120 tokens. Peak QPS 40. Budget target is to keep host-related inference spend under $60k/month.
[01:20] Olivia (Finance): That $60k needs to include any reserved capacity commitments or at least show TCO.
[01:26] Priya: Understood. Quick back-of-envelope: hosted per-token price depends on model family — roughly $0.00004 to $0.0002 per output token for mid/large open models on our hosted tier, varies. With continuous batching and KV caching, effective cost per generated token can drop significantly for repeated prefixes.
[01:45] Marcus: Can you break that down? Like, if we do dedicated with a 1-year commit, what's the delta?
[01:50] Liam: Sure. Example numbers — these are illustrative: hosted might be $0.00012/token for a large Llama-style model. Dedicated reserved capacity could be ~40-60% lower per-token depending on utilization because you're amortizing GPUs. Private has similar unit costs to dedicated for the runtime but you'll add on-prem infra and ops. Batching and caching can reduce effective spend by 20-60% depending on workload mix.
[02:12] [00:02:12] Evelyn: 20-60% is a big range — how do we know where we land?
[02:16] Priya: It depends on prompt reuse and sequence length. If you have many requests that share prefix like system instructions or retrieval augmented prompts with same context, KV cache saves tokens and compute. For pure generation with long unique prompts, batching helps but less caching benefit.
[02:29] Marcus: Our typical pattern is retrieval + prompt template; so there's a lot of shared prefix but also variable chunks.
[02:35] Priya: That's ideal for caching. Example: if 40% of tokens are repeatable prefix, then KV cache could reduce billable compute tokens by ~40% for those requests. Batching improves GPU efficiency at the cost of a small latency hit — we can configure aggressive batching for non-latency-critical routes.
[02:50] Tom: Latency SLOs matter — we have user-facing chat that's 300ms target. Can you hit that with dedicated?
[02:55] Priya: Yes, with dedicated and proper provisioning you can meet 200-350ms for typical chats. Hosted can also hit those numbers but with variable multi-tenant noise. Private on-prem can be tuned but requires more ops.
[03:06] [00:03:06] Olivia: On procurement, we need a clear comparison: month-to-month hosted price, 12-month reserved dedicated price, and private TCO. Also any minimum commitments.
[03:14] Liam: We'll send a pricing deck that includes per-token hosted, per-token equivalent for dedicated at different utilization rates, and a simple TCO worksheet for private.
[03:21] Evelyn: Also curious about model variants — do you auto-fall back to smaller models to save cost?
[03:25] Priya: We have smart routing policies. You can route low-criticality traffic to cheaper quantized variants or smaller family models. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles; typical savings from int8 quantization are 30-50% on cost with minor quality tradeoffs that we can measure.
[03:40] Marcus: What about GPU instance types? If we commit to dedicated, do we pick GPU SKU?
[03:44] Liam: Yes, you can specify capacity profile. We recommend a mix depending on model family and latency/throughput needs. We'll propose a configuration in the follow-up benchmark plan.
[03:53] [00:03:53] Evelyn: For the benchmark, what do you need from us?
[03:57] Priya: Token distribution, QPS curve (peak/min), example prompts, and an eval set for quality. We'll run a profiling run to estimate effective tokens after caching, batching gains, and then give a projected monthly cost for hosted vs dedicated.
[04:10] Tom: If we run the benchmark on our data, can you run it in hosted or dedicated?
[04:14] Priya: We can run an initial hosted benchmark, but for dedicated-level numbers we'd spin up a temporary dedicated pool (or simulate) to show utilization-based cost. For private, we'd provide an on-prem runbook and guidance; we can also run a pilot if you have on-prem capacity.
[04:27] Olivia: Security — SOC 2, KMS support, SSO. We need to confirm no customer data is used for model training and retention policies.
[04:34] Liam: Yes. Redwood offers SOC 2 reports, can integrate with your KMS or customer-managed keys in Private, and for Hosted we have contracts/terms ensuring no training on customer data. We'll send the security pack.
[04:44] Marcus: Slight transcription glitch — did you say "KV cache" saves tokens at generation or just speeds up?
[04:49] Priya: It both speeds up and reduces compute by reusing KV cache for prefix tokens so the model doesn't recompute those, effectively lowering billable compute on the backend. In some cases we only bill for the new tokens post-cache depending on config.
[05:02] [00:05:02] Evelyn: Procurement timeline — we aim to decide by end of month; approval in two weeks ideally. Is that feasible?
[05:08] Liam: Yes, we'll prioritize. I'll get pricing over by Thursday.
[05:11] Tom: One objection from infra: we've built internal inference that avoids egress costs and keeps everything in house. Why should we pay for Redwood vs continuing to run on-prem?
[05:20] Liam: Good question. Two arguments: one, operational cost and time-to-market — Redwood's runtime and Optimize tooling often reduces engineering time and provides predictable unit economics so you might save on ops FTEs. Two, for many customers the mixed approach (private for sensitive data, hosted for burst) gives the best TCO. We'll model both.
[05:36] Priya: Also you'll get features like automatic KV caching, rollout policies, and observability out of the box which are nontrivial to build and maintain.
[05:43] Olivia: Finance needs an example TCO for 12 months with 70% utilization on dedicated.
[05:48] Liam: We'll include that scenario. We'll show break-even point vs hosted monthly.
[05:53] [00:05:53] Marcus: Any hidden costs — e.g., data egress or storage for KV cache?
[05:58] Priya: For hosted, standard egress rules apply per cloud provider. KV cache storage is lightweight; for dedicated/private the cache lives on the serving nodes. We'll call out network/storage costs in the TCO.
[06:09] Evelyn: What about quality regressions when you quantize? We need to track metrics.
[06:13] Priya: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets. We can run quantization A/B tests on your eval set so you can see delta in perplexity/accuracy and roll back automatically.
[06:26] [00:06:26] Tom: If we go dedicated, what's the minimum commit?
[06:29] Liam: Typical commitments start at a few hundred thousand a month equivalent for enterprise offers. We can be flexible for pilots — e.g., short-term reserved pool for the benchmark.
[06:36] Evelyn: Ok — can you give a quick worked example with our numbers? 2M requests, avg 300 tokens total per request (prompt+response).
[06:44] Priya: Sure. 2M * 300 = 600M tokens/month raw. If we assume 40% prefix repeatable and KV cache removes those tokens from billable compute, you're down to ~360M billable tokens. If hosted rate is $0.00012/token -> $43,200/month. With batching and dedicated 50% lower at 70% utilization -> ~$21,600/month. Add network/storage and overhead, maybe private TCO edges to $25-30k depending on infra.
[07:11] Olivia: That looks promising. But we need the assumptions spelled out in a spreadsheet.
[07:14] Liam: We'll send the spreadsheet.
[07:16] [00:07:16] Marcus: One more thing — how do you account for embeddings / vector store costs? We use embeddings for retrieval and that'll be a recurring cost too.
[07:23] Priya: We'll split costs: embeddings generation, rerank, and generation. Embedding calls are usually cheaper per token but can add up; we'll show combined per-conversation cost in the sheet.
[07:33] Tom: Any recommended quick wins to reduce cost without sacrificing quality?
[07:36] Priya: Use quantized smaller model for lower-criticality flows, aggressive KV caching for retrieval-heavy paths, and smarter prompt engineering to reduce unnecessary tokens. Also enable per-route batching config.
[07:48] [00:07:48] Evelyn: Alright. Let's wrap with recap.
[07:51] Liam: Recap: we'll send pricing deck + TCO workbook, batching/caching benchmark plan, SOC2/security pack, and propose a short dedicated pilot/demo. Action items: see earlier. Any final questions?
[08:03] Olivia: Nothing else from finance.
[08:05] Marcus: No.
[08:06] Evelyn: Thanks — appreciate the quick math. Looking forward to the spreadsheet.
[08:09] Liam: Great; we'll follow up. Thanks everyone.
